answer.rationale: Negotiation at the previous renewal recovered real margin and moved the incumbent on price and payment terms (memory_c4), while multi-year commitments unlocked volume pricing without narrowing service scope (memory_c6). Renewing without change preserved integration stability and delivery continuity (memory_c1), but risks missing the mandated 18% spend reduction. Negotiating terms directly targets the cost objective, can be executed within the 14-day window, and avoids disruption to the 94%-utilized assembly line with no buffer—unlike switching vendors or adding a second source, which introduce unacceptable delivery risk under current constraints.
